title: Client SDK runtime compatibility checklist and sample patches
author: Ayesha Rao
content:
Summary:

This page documents a pragmatic, repeatable checklist for validating Redwood client SDK builds against supported runtime environments and a lightweight sample-patch workflow for quickly fixing and shipping compatibility patches. The intent is to reduce first-touch failures for new users, improve reproducibility across macOS/Linux/Windows CI images, and provide a clear onramp for partner integrations that ship custom adapters.

Why this matters:
- Developer onboarding friction is the leading cause of trial drop-off. We measure a target: 90% of new SDK users should get a working sample app within 60 minutes.
- SDK runtime incompatibilities (binary/ABI changes, transient TLS/runtime dependency mismatches, packaging differences) account for ~45% of early support tickets.
- A small, documented patch path reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) for SDK regressions from days to hours.

Scope and assumptions:
- This checklist focuses on client-side SDKs (Node, Python, Go, Java) that interact with the Redwood API via REST/HTTP streaming and websockets.
- We assume existing CI for each SDK that can run on standard runners (Ubuntu 22.04, macOS 12+, Windows Server 2019+).
- This guide does not cover server-side runtime changes for the serving runtime (see eng-serving-runtime).

Owners and SLAs:
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (SDK stability pod).
- Backup owner: eng-sre (CI environment maintenance).
- Operational SLA: triage start within 4 hours for SDK regressions marked P1; patch published to npm/pypi/proxy repo within 48 hours for high-impact fixes.

Compatibility checklist (run for every release and for each supported runtime):
1) Local smoke test (developer laptop)
   - Clone the sample repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git && cd samples/basic-chat-client
   - Install using documented command for the runtime (example below).
   - Confirm an end-to-end chat sample produces a coherent streaming response and the telemetry ping appears in devx telemetry (event: sdk.sample_run).
   - Expected result: success exit code 0, last-stream token > 0.

2) CI matrix run (minimum matrix)
   - Node: 16.x, 18.x, 20.x
   - Python: 3.9, 3.10, 3.11
   - Go: 1.20, 1.22
   - Java: 17, 21
   - OS: ubuntu-22.04, macos-12, windows-2019
   - Tests: unit (fast), integration (calls against test sandbox), streaming (10s timeout), TLS handshake test.

3) Dependency & packaging verification
   - Verify package manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, pom.xml) list minimum supported versions only.
   - Ensure lockfiles are updated where applicable.
   - Confirm package sizes are within known bounds (Node < 5MB gzipped for core package).

4) Network and TLS compatibility
   - Confirm SDK uses our canonical TLS root bundle and honors system proxies.
   - Run curl -Iv against api-dev.redwood.local to validate TLS cipher compatibility when connecting from each CI image.

5) Streaming and backpressure
   - Run streaming harness with artificial slow consumer and confirm client-side backpressure and reconnect behavior matches the SDK contract (see expected behavior matrix).

6) Telemetry contract
   - SDK must emit telemetry events with fields: sdk.name, sdk.version, runtime.os, runtime.version, sample_id.
   - Verify a telemetry ingestion test: echo "{"sdk.name":"redwood-js","sdk.version":"X.Y.Z"}" | http POST http://telemetry-test.local/ingest and assert 200.

7) Windows-specific checks
   - Path length resilience (long path tests), CRLF handling in sample files, certificate store access for TLS verification.

8) Binary compatibility & native deps (if present)
   - Build native modules on the CI runner and ensure prebuilt artifacts exist for our supported images; otherwise validate dynamic build flow.

9) Multi-arch packaging (optional)
   - If we ship wheels or prebuilt binaries, confirm x86_64 and arm64 artifacts in the release.

10) Security & license checks
   - Run license-scan and SCA (software composition analysis). No critical CVEs outstanding.

Checklist templates (CLI snippets)
- Node smoke install and run:
  npm ci --prefer-offline
  node samples/basic-chat-client/index.js --apiKey $REDWOOD_API_KEY

- Python venv test:
  python -m venv .venv
  source .venv/bin/activate
  pip install -U pip
  pip install -e .
  python samples/basic_chat_client/run.py --api-key $REDWOOD_API_KEY

- Telemetry check (devx test proxy):
  curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"event":"sdk.sample_run","sdk.name":"redwood-py","sdk.version":"0.1.2"}' https://devx-telemetry.internal/api/v1/events -k

Expected results and pass/fail signals:
- Smoke test: must complete in < 15s on developer laptop.
- CI integration tests: must pass across >= 90% of matrix cells. Failures in >10% require triage.
- Telemetry contract: ingestion confirmation within 2s.

Sample patch workflow (low-friction path for compatibility fixes)
1) Reproduce and classify
   - Tag the ticket with runtime labels (node/python/windows/native). Add reproducer gist or minimal Dockerfile.
2) Create hotfix branch: sdk/<lang>/compat/<short-description>
3) Minimal local patch and unit test (target single failing matrix cell)
   - Use the sample-patch template in /repo/ops/patch-templates/sdk-compat.patch
4) CI: run targeted matrix for the failing cell only (use github action filter inputs).
5) Canary publish to internal registry/proxy
   - Node: npm publish --registry https://registry-internal.redwood.local --tag canary-compat
   - Python: twine upload --repository-url https://pypi-internal.redwood.local dist/* --verbose --skip-existing
6) Validate with integration test harness (runs against canary package) for the failing environment.
7) Produce a short changelog entry and release note. If fix addresses security or privacy issues, escalate to security@redwood for review prior to public release.
8) Promote to mainline release when canary passes 3 independent CI runs across different images. Tag release with semver patch bump.
9) Post-release: update compatibility matrix in this doc and notify support and product channels.

Rollback criteria:
- If telemetry errors spike > 3x baseline for the SDK version in the first 30 minutes after release, initiate rollback.
- If > 5% of CI integration jobs fail in the 2 hours post-promotion, revert the release and open a postmortem.

Developer-facing examples (small diffs):
- Node TLS fallback (example change):
  // BEFORE: default agent
  const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true });
  // AFTER: explicit secureOptions and custom CA for older OSes
  const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, secureOptions: crypto.constants.SSL_OP_NO_TLSv1 });

- Python urllib3 retry patch (example):
  from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
  RETRY = Retry(total=3, status_forcelist=(429, 502, 503, 504), backoff_factor=0.5)

Operational telemetry to monitor after any compatibility patch:
- sdk.release.promote (event) with fields: sdk, version, tag, owner
- sdk.error.rate (counter) broken down by runtime.os and runtime.version
- sdk.telemetry.latency.p95 for the ingestion endpoint
- support.ticket.inflow for label: sdk-compat

Related runbook snippets (where to escalate):
1) If reproducer shows native build failures: tag eng-integrations and eng-infra for runner images.
2) If TLS handshake fails across many OS images: escalate to security-and-compliance and eng-sre.
3) If package registry upload fails: contact pkg-team@redwood for registry health checks.

Appendix A — Example compatibility matrix (text table)
| SDK | Supported runtimes | Minimal CI images | Notes |
| redwood-js | Node 16,18,20 | ubuntu-22.04,macos-12,windows-2019 | ensure openssl >= 1.1.1 |
| redwood-py | Python 3.9-3.11 | ubuntu-22.04,macos-12 | link against system cert store on macOS |

Appendix B — Quick triage checklist for support engineers
1) Ask for reproducible steps and the exact SDK version.
2) Request full sdk.debug_logs (enable with REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1).
3) Run the sample with a known-good API key in our dev sandbox.
4) If failure reproduces, open a hotfix branch and follow sample patch workflow.
